title: Best Places to Visit in Shimla, Complete Travel Guide from Delhi & Beyond
content:
Shimla - Himanchal Pradesh, 

Shimla, famously known as the “Queen of Hills,” is a magical hill station in Himachal Pradesh that attracts travelers all year round. Imagine waking up to a gentle mountain breeze, surrounded by tall pine trees, with snow-capped peaks glistening in the distance. Walking down its winding lanes, you’ll discover colonial-era buildings, charming churches, and vibrant local markets. Shimla is a perfect blend of history, nature, and modern tourist facilities.

Once the summer capital of British India, Shimla still carries the elegance of that era. You can stroll through the Mall Road, enjoy a cup of coffee at a cozy cafe, or admire the iconic Christ Church, all while soaking in the cool mountain air. But Shimla is not just about history; it’s also a hub for adventure and leisure. Trekking, horse riding in Kufri, skiing in nearby Narkanda, or just relaxing in scenic viewpoints—Shimla offers experiences for every kind of traveler.

Families love its peaceful walks and scenic picnic spots, couples adore its romantic charm, and solo travelers enjoy the easy accessibility and safety of this hill station. The Kalka - Shimla toy train, a UNESCO World Heritage site, makes the journey even more memorable with its tunnels, bridges, and panoramic views of the mountains.

Shimla is approachable from major cities like Delhi, Chandigarh, and Jaipur, making it ideal for short trips or long vacations. Each season adds its own beauty: cool summers, colorful autumns, and snow-covered winters. No matter when you visit, Shimla leaves an impression that stays long after you’ve left.

How to Reach Shimla:

  • By Air: Jubbarhatti Airport (23 km from Shimla). Better option: Chandigarh Airport (113 km).
  • By Train: Kalka–Shimla toy train is a scenic UNESCO World Heritage journey.
  • By Road: Buses, taxis, and private cars connect Shimla to Delhi, Chandigarh, and Manali.

Best Time to Visit Shimla:

  • Peak Season (March - June): Pleasant weather, perfect for sightseeing, shopping, and family trips. Crowded but lively.
  • Moderate Season (September - November): Clear skies, mild temperatures, and fewer tourists. Ideal for peaceful travel.
  • Low Season (December - February): Snowfall turns Shimla into a fairytale. Perfect for honeymooners and snow adventures.

Distances from Key Cities:

  • Delhi to Shimla: 342 km (7 - 8 hrs by road, 10 hrs by train),
  • Chandigarh to Shimla: 113 km (3 - 4 hrs by road),
  • Manali to Shimla: 248 km (approx. 7 hrs by road),
  • Kalka to Shimla: 96 km (5 - 6 hrs by toy train),
  • Jaipur to Shimla: 601 km (11 - 12 hrs by road),

Things to Do in Shimla:

1- Mall Road & The Ridge - The heart of Shimla, perfect for shopping, enjoying street food, and taking in views of the mountains. Don’t miss the historic Christ Church while strolling here.

2- Kufri - Just 16 km from Shimla, Kufri is famous for horse riding, skiing, and adventure activities. Snowfall here makes it a favorite in winter. click here for more details

3- Jakhoo Temple - Perched on Jakhoo Hill, this Hanuman temple offers panoramic views of Shimla. Watch out for playful monkeys along the way.

4- Christ Church -  One of the oldest churches in North India, with beautiful stained glass windows. A must-visit for history and architecture lovers.

5- Annandale - A scenic meadow area used by the Indian Army. Perfect for picnics, walks, and a peaceful escape from the busy city. 

6- Indian Institute of Advanced Study - Explore British-era architecture in a serene setting. Great for history enthusiasts and photography lovers.

7- Tattapani & River Rafting - Around 50 km from Shimla, Tattapani is known for hot springs and river rafting. A perfect day trip for adventure seekers.

8- Mashobra & Naldehra - Offbeat destinations near Shimla with apple orchards, golf courses, and lush green landscapes. Ideal for nature lovers seeking tranquility.

Top 5 places to visit near Shimla within 50 km:

1. Kufri (16 km)

  • Famous for horse riding, trekking, and skiing in winter.
  • Offers panoramic views of the Himalayan ranges.
  • Ideal for adventure lovers and families alike.

2. Mashobra (12 km)

  • A serene village with apple orchards, forest walks, and nature trails.
  • Great for quiet picnics and photography.
  • Less crowded than central Shimla, making it peaceful.

3. Chail (45 km)

  • Known for the world’s highest cricket ground and Chail Palace.
  • Surrounded by lush forests, perfect for nature walks.
  • A great offbeat alternative for travelers seeking tranquility.

4. Naldehra (22 km)

  • Famous for its scenic golf course and apple orchards.
  • Ideal for horse riding and enjoying lush green landscapes.
  • A calm spot away from Shimla’s hustle and bustle.

5. Tattapani (50 km)

  • Known for natural hot springs and river rafting on the Sutlej River.
  • A mix of adventure and relaxation in one spot.
  • Popular for day trips and short nature escapes.

faqs.question: Why Shimla called the “Queen of Hills”?
faqs.answer: Shimla is called the Queen of Hills because of its breathtaking scenery, colonial charm, and the perfect mix of adventure and relaxation. It’s one of the few hill stations that feels alive yet peaceful at the same time.

faqs.question: Shimla get snowfall every year?
faqs.answer: Yes! Shimla usually sees snowfall from late December to February. Snowfall transforms the town into a winter wonderland, attracting couples, families, and snow lovers.

faqs.question: How many days are ideal for a Shimla trip?
faqs.answer: 3 - 4 days are enough to explore Mall Road, Kufri, Jakhoo Temple, and Christ Church, with a possible day trip to Mashobra or Chail. A week-long stay allows you to relax and explore at a slower pace.

faqs.question: Shimla good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Snowfall, cozy mountain hotels, and romantic walks on Mall Road make Shimla a perfect honeymoon destination, especially in winter.

faqs.question: Shimla safe for solo or female travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes. Shimla is considered safe, but it’s always good to avoid deserted areas at night and follow local safety precautions.
